text: AESO, Large Load Integration Phase 2A BYOG Process Update, stakeholder session deck (18 Jun 2026, updated 24 Jun 2026). About 20 GW of data-centre load requested each quarter since Q2 2025 (19.2 GW Q2 2026). Phase 2 is modular: 2A BYOG, 2B ISO tariff, 2C "Grid Partners" (flexible load structures, operating procedures, market products), not yet set. Load management: data centres prioritized above other loads for reduction under supply-related conditions; in standard operation, if firm load shed is needed in an emergency, data centres reduce before all other firm loads; procedures (pro rata, blocks, rotations) to be developed. 74.9 MW applications rose from 9 (Jun 2025) to 18 (Jun 2026) in the 25–75 MW band; AESO may lower the 75 MW threshold. Distribution-connected large loads bypass BYOG; AESO has limited tools for them. Final process was planned for late July–early August 2026 — https://aesoengage.aeso.ca/pre-engagement-phase-ii-large-load-integration

AESO Update on Data Centres (Sep 2025): over 20,000 MW of data-centre load on the AESO project list; Phase 1 qualified 15 projects / 5 developers / 4,800 MW and assigned 1,200 MW to 3 projects / 2 developers, contracts pending execution (deadline extended to Oct 2025 for the provincial levy engagement); draft technical connection requirements for transmission-connected data centres posted 22 Aug 2025, final requirements planned Nov 2025 — https://aesoengage.aeso.ca/pre-engagement-phase-ii-large-load-integration

Data Centre Regulation, Alta Reg 117/2026 under the Electric Utilities Act (King's Printer extract, current as of 9 Jun 2026; J.B. PDF 16 Oct 2026). s. 1: data centre includes hosting/cloud, digital asset mining, AI/ML, content delivery. s. 2: "large data centre" = maximum demand directly from the transmission system of 75 MW or more, or a lower threshold the AESO sets for reliability. s. 3: AESO may aggregate integrated data centres on the same or adjacent parcels with the same owner or affiliate. s. 5: a large data centre may be "tethered" to new or added generating units or energy storage able to supply at least its maximum demand, reliably and predictably (the Regulation does not limit the fuel; AESO's first intake does). s. 6: tethered requests processed first. s. 7: AESO may require site control, municipal zoning approvals, financing, permits or water licences. s. 8: no service above the tethered supply. s. 9: bridged service before the supply runs only once the plant is approved by the AUC, max 3 years, AESO may cap each and all bridged loads and suspend for unmet criteria. s. 10: inadequate supply — bridged data centres reduced before all other market participants; mandatory load shed — large data centres reduced before all others. s. 12: review by 31 May 2030, expires 31 May 2035 — https://open.alberta.ca/publications/2026_117

text: Edmonton Zoning Bylaw 20001 (Charter Bylaw 20001 as adopted, effective 1 Jan 2024; City PDF, OCR text, J.B. download 14 Oct 2026; later amendments not checked), s. 7.140 Special Information Requirements, subs. 9 Sun Shadow Impact Study: the Development Planner MAY require one only where the development is a Discretionary Development (9.1); prepared by an Alberta P.Eng. or architect (9.2.1); shadows every 3 hours between sunrise and sunset, Mountain Standard Time, on 21 Mar, 21 Jun, 21 Sep and 21 Dec (9.2.3); impact judged as the difference between the maximum massing the zone allows and the proposed massing (9.3.1); may refuse or require redesign (9.3.2–9.3.3). No shadow clause found in the standard industrial zones (BE, IM, IH); shadow clauses appear for towers in RL and MU (in compliance with 7.140), UI height variances, and special areas (HOR, CMU, AED, RTCC, ALA); 3.50 Energy and Technology Park mentions shading only as tree planting. s. 2.140 IH lists permitted uses only (Major Industrial; Minor Industrial limited to those existing at 1 Jan 2024) and no discretionary uses, so the study cannot be required there; the bylaw names no data-centre use (Minor/Major Industrial definitions, Part 8), so the use class is for the Development Planner to determine. Search of the full text for shad/shadow/sun — https://zoningbylaw.edmonton.ca/

Edmonton Zoning Bylaw 20001 (as adopted, effective 1 Jan 2024; later amendments not checked), s. 2.250 FPO Floodplain Protection Overlay: applies to the lands mapped in its Appendix I (floodplains of the North Saskatchewan River and tributaries), and to the whole lot if the boundary crosses it (2.2); the applicant must submit an Alberta P.Eng. or architect certificate that the development complies with the floodplain policies of the applicable statutory plans (3.1); the Development Planner may require the geodetic elevation of the building and of its lowest opening, and confirmation that habitable rooms, electrical panels, heating units and operable windows are flood-proofed, plus basement and site drainage (3.2); conditions must follow the certificate (3.4). The bylaw sets no flood construction level of its own (Vancouver: FCL 4.6 m) — the level comes from the statutory plans or provincial flood mapping — https://zoningbylaw.edmonton.ca/
